correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact mu(C5) graph on originals 0..4, clones 5..9 and apex 10; all 20 edges and full ten-element D5 action follow from degree classes and pentagon automorphisms. An independent implementation (distinct from verify.py) enumerated all matchings with simplex counts (20,135,365,360,87), rebuilt oriented simplex boundaries and calculated ranks (19,116,249,87) over F2 and F101. Because d1<=20-1=19, d2<=135-rank(d1)=116, d3<=365-rank(d2)=249, d4<=87, modular lower bounds force identical rational ranks. Thus reduced H3 has rank 360-249-87=24 and all other reduced rational groups vanish, not just a mod-prime assertion. Independently computed all 10 signed fixed-face trace vectors: identity (20,135,365,360,87), each nonidentity rotation (0,0,0,0,2), each reflection (2,-3,-5,0,1). Signed reduced Lefschetz then gives H3 character (24,-1,0). The rational character is exactly 2 regular D5 plus Q(zeta5) (reflection acts by conjugation). Finite rational semisimplicity gives module isomorphism; averaging yields D5-invariant dimension 2 and C5-invariant dimension 4; rational orbit-space cohomology equals group invariants. The independent computations exhaust all simplices and 10 automorphisms of this ONE finite graph, and a fresh SHA-1 Git tree rebuild matches the assigned source tree. No integral representation or homotopy quotient claim is inferred.

value.rationale: The Grötzsch graph is a canonical smallest triangle-free 4-chromatic graph with intrinsic full dihedral symmetry; the natural action on the ordinary matching complex yields an exact rational representation invariant. The earlier 24-dimensional nonequivariant H3 is insufficient to determine rotation/reflection signs, its rational irreducible decomposition, or the Betti number of the symmetry quotient. Computing the complete module 2Q[D5]+Q(zeta5) and a two-dimensional invariant sector fills a motivated, previously undetermined exact structural gap. The exact single-graph classification is mathematically useful in equivariant combinatorial topology without claiming a family theorem or paper-sized downstream result.

limitations: One specific eleven-vertex graph, only reduced rational simplicial homology and coarse quotient; integral lattice and equivariant homotopy not asserted.
Exact finite exhaustive verification covers all faces of this finite graph; finite-field rank equals rational rank here only by the explicit matching upper-bound proof.
Literature assessment bounded; no global priority or external peer-review certification.
residual_risks: Bounded best-of-knowledge priority only: unindexed or unpublished exact D5 character computations for this particular graph could exist.
Cohomology of the nonfree finite-group quotient uses the standard rational finite-group averaging theorem; the claim is about rational, not integral, quotient homology.
The independent verification checks finite source-defined chain complexes; it does not establish integral D5 lattice, equivariant wedge splitting, or wider Mycielski families.
